flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 puts it at risk of attack from the white pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e6.
flags.critique: This game is an Albin Countergambit and you just told me the defining move is a hanging pawn I should have tucked back to e6. I came here to learn the idea — give White a pawn, jam d4, develop with tempo — not to hear that ...e5 is a piece-safety inaccuracy. Engine prefers the QGD, fine, but 'the pawn is under attack' is not a lesson, it is a recapture I already see.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: e5 is defended by the d5 pawn. Calling it undefended is a lie; I would recapture in a heartbeat if I did not know ...d4 exists. The queen-on-d5 bit is real, but you buried it under a SEE slogan that a 1000 can refute by counting defenders.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: I did not 'save a pawn.' I declined the recapture on e5 and rammed a wedge onto d4 — that is the whole Albin. Recapturing also saves the pawn. If your because-clause cannot tell those apart, I learned nothing about why this opening exists.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is playable, but moving your pawn to a3 would be better.
flags.critique: a3 would be better why? This is the named Normal Line and you still will not tell me a3 stops ...Bb4+. 'Playable, but a3' with empty reasons is a coin flip, not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to b4 is the strongest move because it attacks the king directly.
flags.critique: It is check. I know it attacks the king; that is what the plus sign means. Teach me the tempo — develop, drag their bishop to d2, mess up their queenside — or skip the sentence.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d2 with your b4-bishop is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: Which white pawn? Name the square or do not talk. I traded a checking bishop; if the point is that e3 loses a defender so ...dxe3 works, say e3. 'The defender of the white pawn' is a template with the serial numbers filed off.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d2 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended and then pin the pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: That sentence is broken English, and 'the bishop was undefended' is just 'you recaptured.' The pin of d4 to the queen is the only thing worth teaching and you glued it on with 'and then pin' like a second verb wandered in.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d8 with your queen puts it at risk of attack from the black king and c6-knight. A better move would have been taking the pawn on e3 with your queen because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I traded queens. The king and knight recapturing is the exchange, not me hanging my queen. Qxe3 keeping queens and pocketing the pawn is the real lesson — do not dress a queen trade up as piece-safety.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but castling kingside gives your king too little room on the back rank. A better move would have been moving your d8-knight to c6.
flags.critique: I castled. You lectured me about back-rank room like I just walked into a mate net. If Ndc6 is better because the knight is still sitting on d8, say that. Do not invent a king-safety crisis for a normal O-O.

flags.quote: Moving your f3-knight to g5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You jumped a knight at the e6 bishop and toward f7/h7, then shrugged. 'Strongest move' with no because is a sticker, not a coach. Tell me I am attacking the bishop and fishing for Nxe6 or kingside pressure.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to f5 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Ng5 was hitting the bishop, not a pawn. I moved the bishop so it would not get taken or swapped on e6. If your saves-piece line cannot tell a bishop from a pawn, I cannot trust a word you say about hanging pieces.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is a mistake, but moving your f5-knight to h6 would be better.
flags.critique: I kicked the knight on g5 and you answered with 'mistake, but Nh6' and zero why. Same square, opposite idea, no threat, no structure. That 'but' sentence is how you admit you have no lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 leaves your g5-knight hanging to the black pawn. A better move would have been moving your g5-knight to e4 because it saves your e4-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The hanging-knight half is the first honest sentence in a while. Then you tell me Nge4 'saves your e4-knight' — there is no knight on e4 until I move there. You named the destination as if it were already hanging. I am not saving an e4-knight; I am running away from ...hxg5.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e6 with your d8-knight hands the opponent the advantage because the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been taking the knight on g5 with your h-pawn because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: You blamed the blunder on taking a free pawn. That is backwards: taking free stuff is usually the point. The crime is leaving the hanging knight on g5. hxg5 is correct in the second sentence, then you sabotage the first with 'because the pawn was undefended' like greed is the explanation instead of the missed piece.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e6 with your g5-knight is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black f8-rook.
flags.critique: I recaptured a knight. Nobody is taking the f8 rook next. 'Defender of the f8-rook' is removed-defender firing because the knight happens to touch f8. Recapture the piece; do not invent a rook hunt.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e4.
flags.critique: g4 kicks the knight on f5. That is the move. You talked about a backward pawn to defend, which is jargon I cannot even parse as English. If g4 is wrong, tell me the knight comes in or my king file opens — do not hide a pawn kick behind structure bingo.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to e7 is a mistake, but moving your knight to g3 would be better.
flags.critique: g4 just hit my knight. Ne7 runs home; Ng3 hits the undefended rook on h1. That is a tactic. You said 'Ng3 would be better' like a tooltip and listed saves-piece on the retreat. I needed 'go to g3 and take the rook,' not a silent alternative.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You jammed a pawn onto h6 in their king's face and had nothing to say. Passed pawn, wedge, promotion threat, cramp — pick one. Bare 'strongest move' on a pawn that close to queening is malpractice.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h7 is a mistake because it gives you a passed pawn and it puts the opponent in check. A better move would have been moving your knight to e4.
flags.critique: A mistake because it gives me a passed pawn and a check? Those are compliments. You used the good-things list as the because-clause for a bad move. The actual lesson is the pawn gets stuck on h7, their king hides on h8, and I should have played Ne4 instead of checking with the pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to d8 leaves your pawn hanging to the white d6-rook. A better move would have been moving your pawn to g4 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: g4 saves g5 from the knight on e4, not from the rook on d6. You named the wrong attacker. If c6/e6 were the hanging pawns, g4 does not save them. Pick a pawn, pick the piece that takes it, and stop mixing files.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c6 with your d6-rook leaves your king with less protection. A better move would have been taking the pawn on g5 with your knight because you take the defender of the black pawn.
flags.critique: My king is on c1. The rook left d6, not a shield in front of me. This was grabbing the wrong pawn — Nxg5 is the capture — and you invented king safety plus another nameless 'defender of the black pawn.' I cannot act on a defender you will not name.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to g5 is playable, but moving your pawn to b3 would be better.
flags.critique: b3. In this position. With no because. I would rather you stay quiet than recommend a queenside pawn nudge like it is a secret code. If b3 stops a knight jump or makes luft, say it.

flags.quote: Moving your d8-rook to d7 is a blunder, but moving your d8-rook to c8 would be better because you skewer the white c7-rook, exposing the white pawn and then pin the pawn to the king.
flags.critique: Eval jumps a thousand centipawns and you never say I put my rook on a square their rook takes. You rattle skewer, exposed pawn, pin-the-pawn-to-the-king — there is a c4 pawn in the way of that 'pin.' I hung a rook (or a recapture that explodes). Start there, not with tactic-word salad on the move I did not play.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d7 with your c7-rook is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer and your rook can use an open file.
flags.critique: I took a free rook. You said king safer and an open file. If hanging and capture are in the reasons, put them in the sentence. This is how I learn to ignore you on the one recapture a child would get right.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c4 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: This is the Queen's Gambit: hit d5, trade a wing pawn for a center pawn. 'Control more central squares' is the same sticker you put on d4. Reasons even include hanging, which never makes the sentence, so I get center-control mush plus a ghost tactic.

suggestions.title: Never praise a classified error
suggestions.detail: select-insight sets explainPlayedAsBenefit for concept check and capture, so a checking mistake (h7+) and a capturing blunder (Nxe6) get playedBecause from pickBenefitReasons: passed pawn, check, undefended pawn. A 1200 hears 'mistake because it checks / because the pawn was free.' Gate: if classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, becauseReasons must be problemReasons only; drop check/capture from explainPlayedAsBenefit unless the move is best/good. Also stop CONCEPT_PRIORITY from picking check/capture ahead of piece_safety on losses.

suggestions.title: Stop calling defended takes free
suggestions.detail: wins_material copy uses 'the X was undefended' when SEE is near piece value. dxe5 on a pawn guarded by d5, and every recapture, fire that line. Require no legal recapture of equal or higher value, or drop wins_material on even trades. Recapture tautology ('strongest because the piece you just took was undefended') should be stripped in dropTautologyReasons the same way capture already is.

suggestions.title: Name the real piece and attacker
suggestions.detail: saves_piece is labeled on the destination square (Nge4 → 'e4-knight') and sometimes the wrong type (Bf5 'saves your pawn'). ignored_threat on Rad8 named the d6-rook while the better move g4 saves g5 from the knight. In move-copy, ownedPhrase for saves_piece must use the from-square; hanging/ignored_threat problem copy must name both the hanging unit and the attacker that matches the suggested save. Piece type must be the unit actually attacked, not a nearby pawn.

suggestions.title: Name the hanging unit or drop it
suggestions.detail: removed_defender keeps producing 'defender of the white pawn' / 'black f8-rook' / 'the black pawn' on recaptures where nothing newly hanging is the point (Bxd2+, Nxe6, Rxc6). Only emit it when newlyHanging is SEE-negative next ply, and force ownedPhrase to include square and type. Otherwise rank capture or wins_material first so the sentence is 'you recapture' not a phantom defender.

suggestions.title: No silent alternatives or bare strongest
suggestions.detail: e3→a3, h6→Nh6, Ne7→Ng3, Ng5→b3, and Ng5/h6 as 'the strongest move' all ship with empty reasons. If suggestedBecause is null, either pick a ranked benefit (prevent check, kick a piece, passed pawn, hit an undefended rook) or omit the alternative instead of 'X would be better.' If playedBecause is null on best, do not claim strongest — fall back to development/plan or 'one of several strong moves' via margin, never a period after strongest with nothing taught.

suggestions.title: Teach the kick before pawn jargon
suggestions.detail: g4 vs Nf5 and h5/h6 vs Ng5 are pawn attacks on pieces. pickProblemReasons/pickBenefitReasons still lead with backward_pawn. Rank kicked_by_pawn (and the hanging piece it creates) above doubled/isolated/backward/pawn_shield when the moved pawn attacks a piece. Phrase-bank 'creates a backward pawn to defend' is not English a club player can use.

suggestions.title: Lead with the recapture on a 1000cp swing
suggestions.detail: Rd7 → Rxd7 is a rook leaving the board and the copy concatenates skewer+pin follow-ups on Rc8, including a 'pin' through the c4 pawn. If evalLossCp is huge, pickProblemReasons should prefer hanging/refutation_material on the moved piece even when SEE looks equal (recapture fails). describeBecause should not chain likely skewer and pin into one sentence; one tactic, named squares. Suggested Rc8 can say 'challenge the rook on c7' without inventing a skewer through a pawn.

suggestions.title: Don't scold the Albin as a hang
suggestions.detail: On ...e5 and ...d4 the facts layer only sees hanging/saves_piece. Add a gated space-wedge or offered-pawn reason when a center pawn advances past a capture (Albin d-pawn) instead of recapturing, and suppress hanging on the gambit pawn if the engine line still plays the thematic push. A 1200 playing a named opening should hear 'you offer the pawn to plant d4,' not 'put it at risk, play e6.' Opening-book names are optional; the detector can be structural (pawn recapture declined, pawn lands on the 4th/5th in the opponent half).

whatWorked: dxe3: discovered queen-on-queen is true and specific.
O-O-O: king tuck plus rook to an open file actually describes the move.
e6: the problem clause correctly says the g5-knight hangs to the h-pawn.
g5 hanging to ...hxg5 is the right piece-safety call.
Rd7: rook on the seventh is the real idea, named plainly.
b6: saving the seventh-rank pawn from the rook is accurate.
